name: export-html
reason: initial: the export-html feature of the sample project, one self-contained document from one project object

intent.text: A writer hands the exporter a project object and receives one self-contained HTML document that opens offline from a single file, with every problem in the input reported as a warning instead of a crash, so that publishing a project never depends on a network or on hand-fixing the output.

scope.text: src/export/: the exporter module and everything it needs to turn a project object into HTML.
tests/export/: the behaviour, edge and contract checks and the reference project fixture they run against.
A command-line binary, an export dialog, PDF or Markdown output, and fetching assets over the network: none of these are built; the exporter is a library function only.

constraints.text: Every import in src/export/ is a node: built-in or a relative path inside src/export/; none of node:http, node:https, node:net, node:dgram or node:tls is imported, and fetch is never called.
The exported document references no external location: no src, href, srcset or action attribute value starts with http:, https: or //, and no style contains url( or @import.

interfaces.name: exportProject
interfaces.text: src/export/index.mjs exports exportProject(project, options) where options is {inlineAssets: boolean, default true}; it returns {html: string, warnings: [Warning]} and returns normally for every project object, reporting input problems through warnings.

interfaces.name: Project and Warning
interfaces.text: Project = {name: string, pages: [{slug: string, title: string, blocks: [{type: text | heading | image, text?: string, asset?: string, alt?: string}]}], assets: [{id: string, path: string, type: string, data: base64 string}]}, instantiated by tests/export/fixtures/reference-project.json; Warning = {code: missing-asset | no-pages | unknown-block, message: string, page: slug or null}.

behaviours.text: exportProject returns html that starts with <!doctype html> and contains exactly one <title> element whose text is the project name, HTML-escaped.
Each page in project.pages renders as a <section> whose id attribute is the page slug and whose first child is an <h2> holding the page title, and the sections appear in the order of project.pages.
With inlineAssets true, an image block whose asset id exists renders as an whose src is a data: URI built from the asset type and its base64 data.
With inlineAssets false, an image block whose asset id exists renders as an whose src is the asset path unchanged.
The text of text and heading blocks is HTML-escaped: &, < and > in block text appear in the html as &, < and >, so no block text can open a tag.

edges.text: An image block names an asset id that no asset carries: the image is omitted from the html, warnings gains an entry with code missing-asset naming the page slug and the asset id, and exportProject returns normally.
The project has zero pages: the html still carries the doctype, the title and a body with no <section>, and warnings gains one entry with code no-pages.

A block has a type outside text, heading and image: the block is skipped, warnings gains an entry with code unknown-block naming the page slug and the type, and every other block on the page still renders.

decisions.text: One HTML file with inline styles and inline assets by default, because opening offline from a single file is the point; there is no external stylesheet and no asset folder to ship.
Input problems are returned as warnings and never thrown, because the caller decides whether a missing asset stops a publish; only a project that is not an object is a programming error.

verification.text: Five checks, each run from the repository root. T1 (acceptance): node scripts/export-smoke.mjs exports the reference project with default options and exits 0 only when the html starts with the doctype, references no external location and warnings is empty. T2: node --test tests/export/behaviours.test.mjs proves B1, B2, B3, B4 and B5 with one named test per behaviour. T3: node --test tests/export/contract.test.mjs proves I1 and I2 against the fixture. T4: node --test tests/export/edges.test.mjs proves E1, E2 and E3 with one named test per edge. T5: node scripts/export-invariants.mjs proves C1 and C2 by scanning src/export/ and the exported html; it runs at gates only. The end-to-end proof is T1.

acceptance.text: T1 to T5 pass at the frozen map's commit with their raw output on the evidence page, the diff touches only src/export/ and tests/export/, and the owner opens the exported reference project from a single file with no network and sees every page in order.
